title: the-first-shim-starts-the-ground-loop
owner: codemother owns the care of this seam (ruling 2026-09-06); CC/Opus builds. The ground loop package is not touched by this ticket (falsifier tooth 3).
intention: Every shim, on start, checks whether the instance's ground loop is running and launches it if not — so the heartbeat is lazy-inited by the first thing that needs a pulse and by nothing else.
why: Akien's launch chain, told for the second time 2026-09-06 and recorded verbatim at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md. Cast the same day so the intention carries a ticket (CLAUDE.md: an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect).
traces_to: Law 1 (the shim already knows whether it has a pulse; asking anyone else re-derives it) and Law 6 (the loop's liveness is the loop's owned fact and is READ, not scanned); the ground_loop charter's 'any entry point gains the only-once guarantee by spawning the runner — a CALL, not a policy'. Akien 2026-09-06 verbatim: 'all shims, on start, check to see if the ground loop is running. if it's not, the shim launches the ground loop.'

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate — cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_shim_starts_the_loop.py (new): isolated HOME, DEAD→LIVE in one beat, two shims → one loop, ground_loop package untouched (git diff --stat). Feeds back on failure naming the tooth. Durability: committed in cairn; tester seal with source_fingerprint over tools/base.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when: (1) with no loop running (liveness DEAD, no cairn-ground-loop unit), a single `cairn <device> show status` leaves liveness LIVE within one beat plus spawn cost; (2) two shims started within the same 100ms leave exactly one loop (the loser's exit-3 refusal is in the log); (3) the shim adds no line to the ground loop package — `git diff --stat cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/` is empty for this ticket; (4) grep across devices/*/shim.py and tools/base/shim.py finds the check in exactly one place, the base. WRONG INTENT if a shim ends up owning any loop state beyond 'did my spawn attempt start it' — that would be a second loop by another name.

questions.a: One named and standing: 'shim start' is one identifiable event in either order of the bus ticket (registration into the bus process, or BaseShim.__init__ today). Load-bearing only for where the lines sit, not for the behaviour; the falsifier tooth 4 (check in exactly one place, the base) holds either way.

One point not wrapped at /intent, now wrapped: what the shim does when the spawn itself fails (no user manager, systemd unreachable). Answer: the superclaude launcher's fall-through (setsid spawn, and the log line SAYS it will die with the caller) is reused verbatim; the shim logs the same three outcomes. Nothing else asserted-wrapped is open.

Consulted the lab. ground_loop charter: 'any entry point gains the only-once guarantee by spawning the runner — a CALL, not a policy' — this is one more caller, same call. launchers charter's superclaude spawn: both call the guarded runner, so both may exist until the shim path is proven; then the launcher's spawn retires (recorded as this ticket's what_dies-later, not now). Akien's bound on the loop's contents (pulse, flags, devices-found list, ever) is untouched by construction. No Law collides.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) where — cairn/tools/base/shim.py, the start/registration path, one function `ensure_ground_loop(now)`; (b) the read — `liveness.read_liveness(now)['verdict'] == 'DEAD'` from cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.liveness, never pgrep; (c) the spawn — copy the systemd-run block from launchers/superclaude (unit cairn-ground-loop, SuccessExitStatus=3, --setenv HOME and PATH, append redirects to ~/.cairn/logs/ground_loop_nohup.log) and its fall-through; (d) the proof — set HOME to a scratch instance, assert DEAD→LIVE and the diff-stat tooth; (e) don't — no import of the loop's runner as a library (spawn the module), no sleep-poll for LIVE beyond one beat (1s ruled cadence). All written into the ticket's how.

constraints: No change to the ground loop's contents: pulse, control flags, devices-found list — ever (Akien 2026-09-06).
One pipe: device → IPC → own shim → bus → addressee's shim → IPC → addressee; the db alone is exempt (volume).
how: In the shim base (cairn/tools/base/shim.py) the start path reads liveness.read_liveness(now); on DEAD it spawns `python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop` as a transient user unit the way launchers/superclaude already does (same systemd-run line, same SuccessExitStatus=3, same fall-through), and the loop's own flock makes a race between two shims harmless. The check keys on the INSTANCE's liveness record, never on the process table and never on the host alone. The superclaude launcher keeps its spawn for now (it is a launch too; the flock reconciles them); it retires when the shim path is proven. NOTHING is added to the ground loop itself — Akien 2026-09-06: nothing in it but the pulse, the control flags, and the devices-found list, ever.

intent.what: Every shim, on start, checks whether the instance's ground loop is running and launches it if not — so the heartbeat is lazy-inited by the first thing that needs a pulse and by nothing else.

challenge.better_approach: A boot-time service (systemd user unit enabled at login) would be simpler and was proposed by CC on 2026-09-06; Akien's chain retires it — the system lazy-inits from the command, and ruling 2026-08-11 already forbids system-level startup. Putting the check in the launcher script instead of the shim was the other candidate; the shim is right because a shim can be started by something other than a launcher (a proof, the web server) and each of those needs the same guarantee.
challenge.prior_art: launchers/superclaude spawns the loop as a transient user unit with a measured, proven line (launchers charter: 24-arm proof test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py; SuccessExitStatus=3, --setenv HOME/PATH, append redirects). guard.claim_singleton makes any second launch safe (ticket an-entry-point-starts-the-loop-only-once). liveness.read_liveness is the one address for LIVE/DEAD at the ruled 5s. This ticket moves the CALL to the shim and reuses all three; it invents nothing.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That 'shim start' is a single, identifiable event once the bus is one process (ticket one-bus-per-instance): under reading (a) the shim starts when it registers into the bus process, so the check fires at registration. If the bus ticket lands first, this becomes a few lines in the registration path; if it lands second, the check sits in BaseShim.__init__ and moves later. Either order works; the builder should not wait on the other ticket.
challenge.real_collision: None. The ground_loop charter says the runner is spawned by 'any entry point' — the shim is one. The superclaude launcher's spawn and the shim's spawn both call the same guarded runner, so they cannot both win. The only rule this must not touch is the ground loop's contents, and the how says so.

why_beneath_the_why: Akien 2026-09-06: 'if everything goes thru one pipe, we learn faster' and 'everythign automatically lazy inits' — the operator types one command and the system stands itself up behind it, on one pipe, with nothing to remember.

decisions.text: shims, on start, check to see if the ground loop is running. if it' not, the shim launches the ground loop. — 'on start' is BaseShim.__init__ (cairn/tools/base/shim.py:96), the one event every shim start shares.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 2: start path named inline (BaseShim.__init__), so D1 does not lean on D4 for where

decisions.text: nothing in the ground loop except the pulse, the ground loop control flags, and the devices-found list. Ever. — so this ticket adds NO line to cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/: `git diff --stat cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/` is empty for this ticket, and that emptiness is a tooth of the proof.

The check keys on the INSTANCE's liveness record and nothing else: `read_liveness(now, home=None)` — which EXISTS today, measured 2026-09-16: `def read_liveness(now, home=None)` at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/liveness.py:82, returning a dict {verdict: 'LIVE'|'DEAD', record: dict|None, age_s: float|None}, and it is not written by this ticket (D2); DEAD when the record is absent or older than STALENESS_THRESHOLD_S=300s) — never the process table, never pgrep, never a unit query. A shim on a second host of the same instance checks the instance's loop, not its host's.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 2: read_liveness stated as existing with its measured address and signature, not assumed

decisions.text: WHERE: one module-level function `ensure_ground_loop(now: datetime, *, home: Path | None = None, log: Path | None = None) -> dict` in cairn/tools/base/shim.py, and ONE call site: the end of BaseShim.__init__ (shim.py:96). Why the constructor: `cairn <device>` today constructs the shim and does nothing else (cairn/devices/tester/0/bin/tester: `shim = TesterShim()` then two prints), so the constructor is the only event every shim start shares until b41b0c0fff0e puts resolve() on the shim. Grep `ensure_ground_loop(` across cairn/devices/*/shim.py finds zero calls — the base is the one place (falsifier clause 4).

RETURN SHAPE: {'verdict': 'LIVE'|'DEAD' as read, 'spawned': 'unit'|'setsid'|'none', 'note': str}; on LIVE it returns {'verdict':'LIVE','spawned':'none','note':'loop LIVE, age <n>s'} and touches nothing — the read is one file open, so a shim constructed a thousand times in a proof costs a thousand file reads and zero spawns while the loop beats. The result is kept on the shim as `self._ground_loop` (a dict, read by the proof) — no method, no property, no emit: the shim owns nothing about the loop beyond 'what did my one attempt do' (the WRONG INTENT clause).

THE SPAWN copies launchers/superclaude:337-346 as one argv list: ['systemd-run','--user','--quiet','--unit',unit,'--working-directory',repo_root,'--setenv=HOME='+home,'--setenv=PATH='+path,'-p','SuccessExitStatus=3','-p','StandardOutput=append:'+log,'-p','StandardError=append:'+log,'--','python3','-m','cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop'] run with subprocess.run(capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30). unit = os.environ.get('CAIRN_GROUND_LOOP_UNIT','cairn-ground-loop') (mirrors superclaude's SUPERCLAUDE_GROUND_LOOP_UNIT — and it is the proof's handle for a unit of its own). repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] (the tree this shim.py sits in; measured: cairn/tools/base/shim.py → parents[3] is the repo). home = HOME as the process sees it (os.environ['HOME']) — the same value read_liveness resolved the record under, so the spawned loop writes the record the shim will read. log = ~/.cairn/logs/ground_loop_nohup.log (superclaude's; one log, where a human already looks).

THE THREE OUTCOMES, decided before anything is logged (superclaude:354-380 mirrored): rc 0 → spawned 'unit'; rc != 0 with stderr matching any of 'already loaded', 'fragment file', 'already exists', 'Unit ' + 'already' → `systemctl --user reset-failed <unit>.service` once and ONE retry of the same argv; a second failure of that kind → spawned 'none' (refused: the name is held, so a loop already holds it; nothing is spawned another way); systemd-run absent (FileNotFoundError) or any other non-zero rc → the fall-through: subprocess.Popen(['python3','-m','cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop'], cwd=repo_root, start_new_session=True, stdin=DEVNULL, stdout=stderr=the log opened for append) → spawned 'setsid'. Every outcome appends one line to the log: '<date -Is> shim <device_id or unborn>: ground_loop: <outcome and systemd-run's own words>'; the refused line says NOTHING was spawned another way (superclaude:383-385's sentence, kept).

NEVER: no import of cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.__main__ or loop as a library (the module is SPAWNED — the runner's own flock is the only-once guarantee, ground_loop charter: 'a CALL, not a policy'); no sleep-poll for LIVE inside ensure_ground_loop (it returns after the spawn attempt; the loop's first beat writes the record on its own clock); no exception escapes it — any OSError/subprocess error becomes spawned 'none' with the error text in note and one log line, so a shim ALWAYS constructs (Law 7: loud in the log, never a silent pass and never a crashed shim).

THE RUNNER'S OWN SHIMS: the ground loop process racks DiscoveredShim instances (loop.py:191/221 → BaseShim.__init__), each of which would call ensure_ground_loop and read DEAD during the loop's first beat. That is harmless by D6/D7 physics (the unit name is held → refused → 'none'; under setsid the spawned second runner loses the flock and exits 3), so no special case is added: the loop is not told it is the loop. Measured cost: one refused systemd-run per racked shim on the FIRST beat only (LIVE thereafter) — 36 subscribers today → 36 refusals logged once per loop start. If the rehearsal or the proof shows that count is a defect it is a new decision line, not a flag.

THE PROOF cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_shim_starts_the_loop.py (new), sealed under the tester: it sets HOME to a scratch dir (so read_liveness resolves a record that does not exist → DEAD) and CAIRN_GROUND_LOOP_UNIT to 'cairn-ground-loop-proof-<pid>' (so the live loop's unit name is not the name it claims); teeth: (1) DEAD before, one BaseShim-subclass construction → _ground_loop['spawned'] in ('unit','setsid') and read_liveness LIVE within 300s = STALENESS_THRESHOLD_S (measured 2026-09-16: the first beat costs ~90-105s on this box and the record is written AFTER the beat, loop.py:269, so 90s is below the floor; a loop that cannot beat once inside the staleness threshold is not LIVE by the record's own definition; polled by the PROOF at 1s, which is the proof's clock, not the shim's); (2) two constructions inside 100ms → exactly one loop: the second's result is 'none' with the refusal in note OR the log shows one exit-3 refusal; (3) `git diff --stat HEAD -- ':(glob)cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/*.py'` is empty (the package's top-level CODE; its proofs/ and validations/ carry another ticket's uncommitted edits today, 77f15, and are not this ticket's to judge); (4) grep over cairn/devices/*/shim.py finds no `ensure_ground_loop(` — only cairn/tools/base/shim.py defines and calls it; (5) with a LIVE record written by hand under the scratch HOME, construction spawns nothing ('none', verdict LIVE). Teardown: `systemctl --user stop <proof unit>` and kill any setsid child, always, in finally.

decisions.text: WATCH: none new — the ticket's cast watchme stands as written; the falsifier's clause (1) is what a later probe would re-run.

BaseShim.__init__ IS the shim-start event this ticket keys on, and the builder does not wait on 48519f4789b1: the constructor is the one event every shim start shares today (measured: cairn/devices/tester/0/bin/tester constructs the shim and does nothing else), and if 48519f4789b1 later moves shim initialization into a registration step, that step still constructs the shim, so the one call site moves with it or not at all — falsifier clause 4 (the check in exactly one place, the base) holds either way. Build now.

TEST FRAMEWORK: none. The proof is a plain script — module-level test_* functions and an `if __name__ == '__main__':` block that calls each in order and prints one green line per tooth; a failed assert propagates and the process exits non-zero. That is how the tester runs every proof (cairn/devices/tester/device.py:108, `runpy.run_path(_proof, run_name='__main__')`), so no pytest, no unittest, and the bare run is `python3 cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_shim_starts_the_loop.py`.

DEVICE ID DOES NOT FLOW into ensure_ground_loop and the log line does not carry it: device_id is an abstract property (shim.py:147) the base cannot read for itself at construction, and D4's signature stands as written (now, home, log — nothing else). The log line is exactly `<date -Is> shim: ground_loop: <outcome and systemd-run's own words>`; the 'or unborn' clause in D7 is withdrawn.

TOOTH 5's LIVE RECORD is written by the package's own write face, never by hand-spelling the schema: `write_liveness(now, {'beats': 1, 'subscribers': []}, os.getpid(), home)` from cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.liveness (liveness.py:60, signature (now: datetime, state: dict, pid: int, home: Path) -> Path; writes <home>/liveness.json atomically, RECORD_NAME='liveness.json' at liveness.py:44), where home = <scratch HOME>/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop — the path instance_home() resolves under that HOME (liveness.py:47 -> address.instance_path('cairn', 0) / 'machines' / 'ground_loop'). The proof mkdir -p's that directory first. now is timezone-aware (datetime.now(timezone.utc).astimezone()) because read_liveness subtracts it from the record's last_run.

LIVE FIRE MEASURED 2026-09-16 18:17:07 MDT: loop DEAD 3.3 days (pid 2132187, beats 2); one `cairn tester` -> cairn-ground-loop.service started by the shim (journal: ExecMainStartTimestamp 18:17:07, ExecStart -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop, pid 2682938); log line 664 'spawn attempted', then 40 refusals at 18:17:07-08 = the loop's own racked shims (D9 predicted 36; 40 subscribers today). The first beat WROTE liveness.json at 18:26:05 (beats 1, pid 2682938, last_pulsed_count 40) — 538s after start — and `cairn groundloop status` read DEAD at 547.8s because write_liveness stamps the beat's START (loop.py:269 passes the beat's now) and the beat outran STALENESS_THRESHOLD_S=300. The 300s bound in D10/D12 holds on a fresh instance (proof: twice green) and NOT on the live one; that is a ground_loop finding (a beat slower than the staleness threshold can never read LIVE), raised to Akien as a question, not this ticket's line to fix (D2).
